questions.prompt: The philosopher himself explained the nature of the stars.
questions.answer: Philosophus ipse nātūram stēllārum explicāvit.

questions.prompt: I saw the queen herself walking through the forum.
questions.answer: Rēgīnam ipsam per forum ambulantem vīdī.

questions.prompt: The soldiers themselves feared the anger of the leader.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs ipsī īram ducis timēbant.

questions.prompt: We gave the gift to the king himself.
questions.answer: Mūnus rēgī ipsī dedimus.

questions.prompt: The words of the poet himself moved the crowd.
questions.answer: Verba poētae ipsīus turbam mōvērunt.

questions.prompt: She herself, though wounded, defended the walls.
questions.answer: Ipsa, quamquam vulnerāta, mūrōs dēfendit.

questions.prompt: The very shoulders of Atlas bear the sky.
questions.answer: Umerī ipsī Atlantis caelum ferunt.

questions.prompt: I trust the physician himself more than his books.
questions.answer: Medicō ipsī magis quam librīs eius crēdō.

questions.prompt: The consul himself led the army across the river.
questions.answer: Cōnsul ipse exercitum trāns flūmen dūxit.

questions.prompt: The maidens themselves wove garlands from wild flowers.
questions.answer: Virginēs ipsae corōnās ē flōribus agrestibus texuērunt.

questions.prompt: He praised the courage of the leader himself.
questions.answer: Virtūtem ducis ipsīus laudāvit.

questions.prompt: I myself heard the philosopher speaking about justice.
questions.answer: Ipse philosophum dē iūstitiā loquentem audīvī.

questions.prompt: The gods themselves favor those who dare.
questions.answer: Dī ipsī audentibus favent.

questions.prompt: We saw the temple itself gleaming with gold.
questions.answer: Templum ipsum aurō fulgēns vīdimus.

questions.prompt: The mother herself carried water to the thirsty children.
questions.answer: Māter ipsa aquam līberīs sitientibus portāvit.

questions.prompt: I will show the letter to the judge himself.
questions.answer: Epistulam iūdicī ipsī mōnstrābō.

questions.prompt: The old man himself, having been summoned, told the whole story.
questions.answer: Senex ipse, vocātus, tōtam fābulam nārrāvit.

questions.prompt: The very roots of the tree were dissolving in the marsh.
questions.answer: Stirpēs ipsae arboris in palūde liquēscēbant.

questions.prompt: They entrusted the city itself to the enemy.
questions.answer: Urbem ipsam hostibus commīsērunt.

questions.prompt: The merchants feared the sea itself more than the storm.
questions.answer: Mercātōrēs mare ipsum magis quam tempestātem timēbant.

questions.prompt: The general himself, arrogant and insolent, despised the auguries.
questions.answer: Dux ipse, superbus et īnsolēns, auspicia contempsit.

questions.prompt: The lungs themselves are strengthened by healthful air.
questions.answer: Pulmōnēs ipsī āere salūbrī firmantur.

questions.prompt: They sacrificed to the goddess herself before the battle.
questions.answer: Deae ipsī ante proelium litāvērunt.

questions.prompt: This I too do myself: out of the many things I have read, I seize on something.
questions.answer: Hoc ipse quoque faciō: ex plūribus quae lēgī, aliquid apprehendō.

questions.prompt: Although indeed not only the fruit but also the very force and nature of the earth itself delights me.
questions.answer: Quamquam mē quidem nōn frūctus modō, sed etiam ipsīus terrae vīs ac nātūra dēlectat.

questions.prompt: This is what happens to people hurrying in a labyrinth: their very speed entangles them.
questions.answer: Quod ēvenit in labyrinthō properantibus: ipsa illōs vēlōcitās implicat.

questions.prompt: The queen herself, though weary, listened to the complaints of the citizens.
questions.answer: Rēgīna ipsa, quamvīs fessa, querēlās cīvium audīvit.

questions.prompt: We entrusted the sacred spear to the priest himself.
questions.answer: Sacram hastam ipsī sacerdōtī crēdidimus.

questions.prompt: The adulterer himself fled the city by night.
questions.answer: Adulter ipse ex urbe nocte fūgit.

questions.prompt: The witness relied on the words of the woman herself.
questions.answer: Testis verbīs mulieris ipsīus frētus est.

questions.prompt: The general himself, having led the army across the mountains, praised the soldiers.
questions.answer: Dux ipse, exercitū trāns montēs ductō, mīlitēs laudāvit.

questions.prompt: You yourself saw the ships burning in the harbor.
questions.answer: Tū ipse nāvēs in portū ārdentēs vīdistī.

questions.prompt: The very walls of the temple trembled at the voice of the goddess.
questions.answer: Ipsī templī parietēs ad vōcem deae tremuērunt.

questions.prompt: The city was betrayed by the guards themselves.
questions.answer: Urbs ab ipsīs custōdibus prōdita est.
